name: Saint Croix
peoples: Indigenous societies including Taíno and Kalinago connections
summary: The island of seven flags—and more than seven episodes of rule.
notes: English, Dutch and French settlements overlapped. The Knights of Malta held proprietary rights under French sovereignty. French evacuation in 1695–1696 ended settlement but not France’s title.

events.title: Spain claims Santa Cruz
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: Rival European settlers
events.detail: English and Dutch settlers established competing footholds.
events.uncertainty: Early settlement dates vary between 1625 and the 1630s; concurrent presence is certain, exclusive ownership is not.

events.title: English settlers gain the upper hand
events.detail: Conflict between colonial settlers ended the Dutch settlement.

events.title: Spanish forces expel the English
events.detail: An expedition from Puerto Rico took the colony.

events.title: France takes Saint Croix
events.detail: French forces displaced the Spanish garrison.

events.title: The Knights of Malta acquire administration
events.detail: The Order purchased proprietary rights in French Caribbean islands.
events.uncertainty: Sources differ on the implementation date and distinguish purchase, lease and administration; French sovereignty continued.

events.title: A French company takes over
events.detail: The French West India Company bought the Order’s rights.

events.title: French settlers evacuated
events.detail: The colonial settlement was abandoned while France retained title.
events.uncertainty: The evacuation is dated 1695 or 1696 in different accounts.

events.title: Denmark buys Saint Croix
events.detail: The Danish West India and Guinea Company purchased the island from France for plantation expansion.

events.title: British occupation
events.detail: War against Denmark brought British forces to the Danish West Indies.

events.title: Britain occupies the Danish islands again
events.detail: The Napoleonic conflict brought a second occupation.

events.title: The Danish government returns
events.detail: The islands were restored following the European peace settlement.

events.title: Denmark sells the islands to the United States
events.detail: The United States paid $25 million in gold; strategic concerns helped drive the purchase.
